newsitem.title: USA: GM earnings jump to $1.8 billion in first quarter. [CORRECTED 19:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: GM earnings jump to $1.8 billion in first quarter. [CORRECTED 19:45 GMT]

text.p: General Motors Corp. said Monday it earned $1.8 billion (corrects from $1.7 billion) in its first quarter, up from $800 million (corrects from $714 million) a year earlier, when its operations were shut down by a brake strike in Ohio.
The year-earlier quarter included a loss of $900 million due to the strike, GM said.
The world's largest automaker said it earned $2.30 a share, up from 93 cents (corrects from 94 cents) in the first quarter of 1996, as its sales grew to $42.26 billion from $39.24 billion.
GM said it was the best quarter in more than 10 years for its North American operations.

"It's clear that we are moving in the right direction to further strengthen the corporation's financial performance," GM Chairman and Chief Executive John Smith said in a statement accompanying the results.
The strike in March, 1996 lasted 17 days at two brake plants in Dayton, Ohio, shutting down 26 of GM's 29 North American assembly plants and numerous components plants.
GM said its North American Operations reported net income of $764 million in the first quarter of 1997, compared with a net loss of $279 million in the first quarter of 1996.
"GM North American Operations' net income of $764 million in the first quarter of 1997 is the best performance for any quarter in more than a decade," Smith said.
Delphi Automotive Systems, GM's automotive parts operations, reported net income of $180 million in the first quarter of 1997, compared with profits of $79 million in the first quarter of 1996.

GM International Operations reported net income of $317 million in the latest quarter, compared with earnings of $432 million in the prior-year period. The most recent quarter included a $55 million after-tax gain related to an agreement with Volkswagen A.G.

"The improved results were driven primarily by the many new models introduced into the marketplace, which are less costly to produce than those they replaced, by continued material-cost reductions, and production efficiencies," Smith said.

GM said its vehicle deliveries in the United States in the first quarter of 1997 totalled 1,123,000 units, resulting in a 30.2-percent share of the U.S. market. That compared with 1,152,000 units and a 31.2-percent share of the U.S. market in the first quarter of 1996.
